topic: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect certification exam preparation - designing and planning cloud solution architecture, managing and provisioning infrastructure, designing for security and compliance, analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes, managing implementation, and ensuring solution reliability on Google Cloud, including the four official case studies
cert_name: Google Cloud Certified - Professional Cloud Architect
exam_format: Approximately 50-60 questions, 120 minutes, delivered online-proctored or at a test center. Multiple choice (single answer) and multiple select in a NON-adaptive, heavily scenario-based format, PLUS questions grounded in four official published case studies (EHR Healthcare, Helicopter Racing League, Mountkirk Games, and TerramEarth). Google uses scaled scoring and does NOT publish an official passing percentage - present pass thresholds as unpublished. The certification is valid for two years. Exam fee is approximately USD 200 (plus tax where applicable) and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Google Cloud pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'; a large share of items are case-study-driven scenarios asking which Google Cloud architecture, service, or design best satisfies a described business AND technical requirement - NOT term definitions
audience: Cloud architects, solution architects, senior cloud engineers, and technical leads who design and manage enterprise solutions on Google Cloud. Google recommends 3+ years of industry experience including 1+ year designing and managing solutions on Google Cloud. Broad familiarity with compute, networking, storage, security, and operations is assumed, as is the ability to translate business goals into architecture. A natural next step from the Associate Cloud Engineer course and a strong companion to the Professional Data Engineer and Professional Machine Learning Engineer courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Translating business AND technical requirements into an architecture: high availability, scalability, cost, performance, and compliance trade-offs; choosing compute (Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run, App Engine, Cloud Functions), networking (VPC design, hybrid connectivity with Cloud VPN/Interconnect, load balancing, Cloud DNS), and storage/data services for a described scenario; migration and modernization planning (lift-and-shift vs re-platform vs re-architect, Migrate to Virtual Machines, database migration); multi-region and DR design; capacity planning and cost modeling. The recurring skill is mapping a case-study's business goals plus technical constraints to the correct GCP architecture.

domains.name: Managing and provisioning a solution infrastructure
domains.notes: Configuring and provisioning the designed solution: network topology (subnets, firewall rules, Shared VPC, VPC peering, Private Google Access, hybrid connectivity), storage systems and data solutions, and compute provisioning. Infrastructure as Code and automation with Deployment Manager, Terraform, and Config Connector; using Cloud Build and deployment pipelines. Choosing the correct provisioning approach and topology for a described requirement, and understanding how the pieces fit together operationally.

domains.name: Designing for security and compliance
domains.notes: Designing secure, compliant architectures: identity and access with Cloud IAM (roles, service accounts, least privilege, workload identity), resource hierarchy and Organization Policy, encryption (Google-managed vs CMEK vs CSEK, Cloud KMS), network security (VPC Service Controls, firewall, Cloud Armor, private access), data protection (Cloud DLP, secrets management), and regulatory/compliance considerations (data residency, HIPAA/PCI/GDPR-style constraints as they appear in the case studies). Choosing the correct security or compliance control for a described scenario.

domains.name: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
domains.notes: Aligning architecture with how the organization works: analyzing and defining technical processes (SDLC, CI/CD, testing/release management, troubleshooting, post-incident review) and business processes (stakeholder management, change management, cost optimization, build-vs-buy, team skill and org constraints). Continuous improvement, observability-driven optimization, and balancing technical debt against delivery. Choosing the process or optimization that best fits a described business and team context.

domains.name: Managing implementation
domains.notes: Advising and overseeing development and operations teams to implement the design correctly: interacting with Google Cloud programmatically (gcloud, Cloud SDK, client libraries, APIs) and via Cloud Shell; ensuring implementation matches the architecture; testing and validation approaches; and applying best practices for reliable, repeatable deployment. Identifying the correct implementation step, API/tool, or hand-off given a described build scenario.

domains.name: Ensuring solution and operations reliability
domains.notes: Operating the solution reliably in production: monitoring, logging, alerting, and profiling with the Cloud Operations suite (Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Error Reporting, Trace); SRE practices (SLIs/SLOs/SLAs, error budgets, toil reduction); deployment and release strategies (blue-green, canary, rolling); disaster recovery, backup, and business continuity; and incident response and post-mortems. Choosing the correct reliability, observability, or DR control for a described operational requirement.

extra_guidance: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect (PCA) is Google's flagship and one of the most valuable, highest-paying cloud credentials, and it is HEAVILY scenario- and case-study-based - the real skill the exam tests is 'given these BUSINESS goals plus these TECHNICAL constraints, which Google Cloud architecture and services are best,' NOT memorizing definitions. CRITICAL: the exam draws a large share of questions from FOUR official published case studies - EHR Healthcare (healthcare SaaS, hybrid-to-cloud migration, compliance/HA), Helicopter Racing League (HRL - live-streaming/media, ML-driven predictions, global low-latency), Mountkirk Games (mobile gaming, GKE, global multiplayer, real-time analytics), and TerramEarth (IoT/manufacturing, connected vehicles, massive telemetry, data pipelines). Devote real coverage to each case study: summarize its business goals, technical requirements, and executive statements, then work through the architecture decisions it drives. Use EXACT current Google Cloud product names: Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Run, App Engine, Cloud Functions, VPC, Shared VPC, Cloud Load Balancing, Cloud Interconnect/VPN, Cloud DNS, Cloud Storage, Persistent Disk/Filestore, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud IAM, Organization Policy, Cloud KMS, VPC Service Controls, Cloud Armor, Cloud DLP, the Cloud Operations suite (Cloud Monitoring/Logging/Trace/Error Reporting), Deployment Manager, Terraform, Cloud Build, and Anthos/GKE Enterprise - with a one-line note that Google's product names evolve, so verify against current docs. The SIX domain names and weights above reflect Google's exam-guide sections; present percentages as APPROXIMATE editorial estimates aligned to the guide and say so where weights appear. Labs are READ-AND-UNDERSTAND architecture walkthroughs (design an HA multi-region web tier, choose GKE vs Cloud Run vs Compute Engine, design a hybrid network with Interconnect and Shared VPC, plan a migration for EHR Healthcare, design the TerramEarth telemetry pipeline, set SLOs and error budgets) - the exam is about architectural judgment, not console clicks; make that explicit. Practice questions MUST be scenario- and case-study-style: compute selection, network topology, migration approach, security/compliance controls, DR/reliability design, and cost/performance trade-offs, with several tied explicitly to the four case studies. Cover classic architect traps: regional vs multi-region trade-offs, Shared VPC vs VPC peering, when to use VPC Service Controls, CMEK vs CSEK, managed instance groups and autoscaling, blue-green vs canary. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 200, varies by region) and note the two-year validity; advise verifying current Google Cloud pricing and the latest exam guide and case studies (Google occasionally rotates case studies). The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 120-minute, case-study-pacing time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
